summary: One account's health at a glance: the score out of 100 in a small ring with its verdict (Healthy, Watch or At risk), how many factors are on track and how the score moved in 30 days. Under it, the four factors (contact, deals on time, win chance and next step) as rows under hairlines, each with its status dot and figure; click one to read its detail right under it. At the foot, the agent's next move with a button: pressing it books or drafts, and the factors it changes update, so the ring and the score move with them. The demo switches between three accounts, one in each state.
use: In a CRM's account sheet or details panel, where a rep needs to know whether an account needs attention and why.
When an agent watches accounts and can take the next step itself, like booking a check-in or drafting an email.
For any score made of a few weighted factors, each with its own status and figure.
features: The score sits in a small ring that fills to it and takes the verdict's colour: green from 70, orange from 50 and red below. The verdict word beside it is in the same colour.
A line such as "Account health, 2 of 4 on track", and the change against the score 30 days ago, such as "−13 in 30 days".
Four full-width rows split by hairlines, each with a status dot, its name, its figure ("11d ago", "0 late", "61%", "None booked") and a chevron. No card, fill or shadow per factor.
The weakest factor that is off track is labelled Weakest in ink beside its name. Colour only marks state, in the dots and the ring.
Clicking a row opens its detail right under it: what happened, and its points out of its maximum. One row is open at a time.

The agent's suggestion is a plain row with the spark icon and a button. Pressing it shows a spinner, then a done chip such as "Booked", and the factors it changed update, for example 58 becoming 78 with Next step turning green.
Switching accounts sweeps the ring and counts the score to the new value, and the words and figures crossfade. An open row stays open on the same factor.
Under 360px of room the agent's button goes under its line, so it fits a narrow sheet. In React, `account`, `onAction` and `open` drive it from your own data.
a11y: The ring is an image labelled with the score, the verdict and the change, such as "Health 58 of 100, watch, down 13 in 30 days".
Each row is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, labelled with its factor, what it means and its status, plus "the weakest factor" where that applies.
A closed detail is hidden and out of the tab order.
The agent's button sets aria-busy while it works, and a polite live region announces what it did. Focus moves to the done chip if it was on the button.
With reduced motion the ring, the score, the crossfades and the opening rows finish at once.

faq.q: How is the score worked out?
faq.a: Each factor has `points` out of its `max`, and by default the score is the points added up, so the maxima should add up to 100 (the demo uses 30, 25, 25 and 20). Pass `score` to show your own number instead.

faq.q: How do I let the agent act?
faq.a: Give the account a `suggestion` and pass `onAction`. Return a promise that settles once the agent is done, then pass the account back with `suggestion.done` set and the factors it changed. The button gives way to a done chip, `doneText` replaces the line, and the ring and score move to the new total.

faq.q: Can I use it in a details sheet that already names the account?
faq.a: Yes. Leave out `name` and the block starts at the score. It is made for a sheet about 440px wide and fits narrower ones too.

faq.q: Can I change the bands and the words?
faq.a: Pass `bands` with the lower bounds for Healthy and Watch (70 and 50 by default), and `verdicts` to rename them. `label` starts the line under the verdict and `period` names the change's period.
